tour.overview:
Upstream from Porto, the Douro river winds between steep hills carved into thousands of terraces of vines. This is where port wine is made, in the oldest demarcated wine region in the world, defined in 1756, and the landscape of the Alto Douro Wine Region is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. For centuries, the wine travelled downriver to Porto in flat-bottomed rabelo boats to age in the lodges of Vila Nova de Gaia.

This private day takes you into the valley with a licensed guide and a vehicle, with two winery visits, lunch and a cruise on the river.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 9 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Porto
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, vehicle and driver; shared or private boat
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Douro viewpoints.
• Two quintas.
• Pinhão and its station.
• The Douro by boat.

WHY THIS WORKS
Your driver handles the winding roads so you can taste, and your guide chooses quintas that suit your tastes.

WHO IT SUITS
Wine lovers, couples and food lovers.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
For the city, choose our Porto walking tour with port cellars.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The harvest takes place in September and early October, when the valley is busiest and most festive. Minimum age for tasting is 18.

days.name: The Douro viewpoints, two quintas, lunch among the vines and a river cruise
days.description:
What to expect: the vineyards and wines of the Douro, with a licensed guide, private vehicle, tastings, lunch and a boat trip.

Your guide and driver collect you at about 8:30 and drive east, about 1 hour 30 minutes, into the valley. You stop at the São Leonardo de Galafura viewpoint, high above the river, where the terraced hills fold away into the distance.

At the first quinta, a family estate, you walk among the vines and see the lagares, the granite tanks where grapes are still trodden by foot at harvest, and taste white, tawny and ruby ports. Lunch is at a quinta with a terrace over the river, with regional dishes and Douro wines.

In Pinhão, the heart of the valley, you admire the station decorated with azulejo panels showing the harvest and the river, and take a one-hour boat trip on the Douro past the terraces and quintas. At a second quinta, you taste Douro reds and whites and a vintage or old tawny port, before driving back to Porto.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:30 – Pick-up in Porto.
10:00 – São Leonardo de Galafura viewpoint.
10:45 – First quinta and tasting.
12:45 – Lunch at a quinta.
14:30 – Pinhão station.
15:00 – Boat trip on the Douro.
16:15 – Second quinta and tasting.
18:30 – Back in Porto.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Harvest experiences, including grape treading, can be arranged in September.
• A private rabelo boat can be booked.

INCLUDED: private vehicle and driver, licensed guide, tastings, lunch with wine, boat trip, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: extra wine and purchases, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Are the tastings included?
faq.answer: Yes, at two quintas, plus lunch with wine.

faq.question: Is the boat private?
faq.answer: The standard boat trip is shared; a private boat can be arranged.

faq.question: Can non-drinkers join?
faq.answer: Of course; quintas offer juices and the landscape is reason enough.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Children are welcome; tastings are for adults over 18.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Largely. Some quintas have steps and slopes.

faq.question: Can wine be shipped home?
faq.answer: Many quintas ship internationally; your guide can help.

faq.question: Can we stay overnight?
faq.answer: Yes, at a quinta in the valley, on a 2-day version.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: No. Buying at the quintas is optional.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Comfortable shoes and layers; summer in the valley is very hot.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: April to October. September is the harvest.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tipping is not obligatory in Portugal, but rounding up or leaving 5 to 10 percent for a guide or driver you were happy with is appreciated.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
